meta.title: Reference-to-Style | AI Collaboration Workspace
meta.description: Turn subjective visual generation into a controllable workflow through failures, product rules, and human evaluation.

hero.title: Reference-to-Style
hero.summary: Translate open-ended style language into content admission, feature compression, and visual-primitive rules while preserving human aesthetic judgment.

sections.label: Core Problem
sections.title: Style language did not define what AI was allowed to reconstruct
sections.summary: “Loose line” described how marks should feel, but it did not prevent scenes, anatomy, and identity features from entering the image. The result still resembled a photo trace.

items.label: Failure signal
items.title: Less detail did not stop reconstruction
items.body: The model continued to complete furniture, continuous body contours, fur, and volume.

items.label: Key judgment
items.title: Decide what to draw before how to draw it
items.body: Content selection, relationship preservation, and identity cues must precede style compilation.

sections.note: Subjective output has no unique answer, but the scope of AI inference can be constrained.

sections.label: Collaboration Method
sections.title: Compress failure diagnosis into three product rules
sections.summary: Failure → Product Rules → Result: the rules control what enters the image, how much information remains, and which visual language may be generated.

items.label: Rule 01
items.title: Content Admission
items.body: Subjects and key interactions may enter. Irrelevant context and unnecessary body information do not enter by default.

items.label: Rule 02
items.title: Feature Compression
items.body: Identity and relationship cues use the minimum sufficient information; preservation does not mean complete rendering.

items.label: Rule 03
items.title: Visual Primitive
items.body: Dots, arcs, open forms, short strokes, overlaps, and blank space limit additional reconstruction.

items.label: Human Evaluation
items.title: Decide final acceptance
items.body: Machines check structure and rules; humans judge identity retention and aesthetic tolerance.

sections.note: Rules constrain the generation boundary but do not automate aesthetic conclusions.

sections.label: Representative Evidence
sections.title: How one failure chain became an acceptable result
sections.summary: The comparison keeps only the clearest failure and a representative pass to show that the rules changed the reconstruction range.

items.label: Human judgment
items.title: Structural compliance is not aesthetic acceptance
items.body: Human Evaluation still confirms whether the key relationship, identity cues, and contextual tolerance are acceptable.

evidence.alt: Early generated result retaining unwanted scene and background structure
evidence.label: Failure
evidence.title: Content Admission failed
evidence.description: The model treated furniture and environmental structure in the source as information that had to remain.

evidence.alt: Sparse-line generated result that passed a representative test
evidence.label: Result
evidence.title: Sparse marks retained the key relationship
evidence.description: Scene content, anatomy, and mark count were constrained while subject identity and interaction remained.

sections.note: The evidence shows a more controllable inference boundary, not that every input will pass consistently.

sections.label: Result
sections.title: Frozen at v0.3.3 with the human judgment boundary intact
sections.summary: Regression showed that the rules reduce uncontrolled reconstruction; mixed outcomes also confirm that final aesthetic acceptance remains human.

items.label: Validated
items.title: Subjective generation can be product-constrained
items.body: Content Admission, Feature Compression, and Visual Primitive form a reusable generation boundary.

sections.note: The product value is an auditable rule and judgment boundary, not a universal prompt.
